notes: PASS RATE UNCHANGED: 95% (20/21) same as iteration-6. The Memento-Skills structural changes (plan + reflection gate) did not break any passing assertions.

SAME WEAK SPOT: Eval 3 'narrows scope' still fails (80%). Agent claims narrowing to 'architecture comprehension' but still covers all 11 hooks, all adapters, all libs. This is a calibration-level issue that the plan/reflection additions don't address — they help DURING investigation, not during scope definition.

SPEED IMPROVEMENT: -38% mean wall-clock time (327.6s → 203.1s). Most dramatic on contradiction (-70%) and vague-calibration (-48%). The investigation plan may help agents converge faster by giving clear direction from the start.
TOKEN INCREASE: +21% mean tokens (58652 → 70789). Agents investigate more thoroughly (more tool calls on cross-module: 13→38) while finishing faster.

CAVEAT: Agents received condensed skill instructions, not the full SKILL.md. The plan/reflection guidance was included but agents did not explicitly verbalize 'Investigation Plan:' or 'Reflection: Continue' in their process. The structural features influence behavior implicitly rather than producing explicit plan/reflection text in output.

QUALITATIVE: Eval 2 output is notably more comprehensive than iter-6 (5 layers vs 3, v4/v5 version comparison, complete code blocks). Eval 4 output is substantially more detailed (417 lines, 3-layer analysis framework, 12-entry source audit). Eval 5 found an ADDITIONAL staleness issue (pre-refactor naming in ide-capability-matrix.md) that iter-6 missed.

PHASE-A CONFIRMATION: Results align with Phase A's finding that the skill is at a quality plateau for assertion-level metrics. The structural changes improve process quality (speed, depth) without moving the pass rate, because the existing assertions already pass at 95%.
